question: Manoj has ₹1230 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Anand and Anil and asked them to invest it at 5% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Anand and Anil got same amount after 12 and 13 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Manoj give to Anil?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When amounts are equal under CI, Ratio of investments P₁ : P₂ = (1 + R/100)Differeⁿce iⁿ Time

Ratio = (1 + 5/100)¹³ − ¹² = 21/20 ⇒ Anand : Anil = 21 : 20

Total parts = 21 + 20 = 41 parts = ₹1230 ⇒ 1 part = ₹30.

Anil's share = 20 parts = 20 × 30 = ₹600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount = ₹1230

Rate of interest (R) = 5% per annum

Anand's time (T₁) = 12 years

Anil's time (T₂) = 13 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount = P(1 + R/100)T
